outline.description: Provides foundational knowledge on diffusion models, their successes in text-guided image synthesis, and the limitations that motivate specialized finetuning.
subtopics: 0.1 What is text-to-image diffusion?
0.2 State‑of‑the‑art diffusion baselines (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, GLIDE, DALL‑E2)
0.3 Limitations of pure text guidance: ambiguity, lack of fine‑grained control
0.4 The two downstream generation objectives studied
0.5 Desired properties of a finetuning strategy
0.6 Overview of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) and Constrained OFT (COFT)

outline.description: Introduces the mathematical tools and prior work that underpin OFT: hyperspherical geometry, energy, and orthogonal transformations.
subtopics: 1.1 Hyperspherical embeddings and cosine similarity
1.2 Hyperspherical energy: definition, intuition, and meaning
1.3 Orthogonal matrices: definition, properties, and role in preserving angles
1.4 Related finetuning techniques (LoRA, adapters, DreamBooth, ControlNet, T2I‑Adapter)
1.5 Key open questions in preserving generative semantic performance

outline.description: Presents the core idea of OFT, why rotating neuron directions is beneficial, and the formal derivation that shows orthogonal transformation preserves hyperspherical energy.
subtopics: 2.1 The role of neuron direction in semantic encoding
2.2 Toy experiments illustrating angular importance
2.3 Orthogonal transformation as the simplest rotational finetuning
2.4 Formal proof: global minimisation of hyperspherical energy via orthogonal maps
2.5 Connection to 2‑D Fourier phase and image semantics
2.6 Why preserving angles safeguards pre‑training knowledge

outline.description: Describes how OFT integrates into the training pipeline, what constraints are imposed, and which layers are targeted.
subtopics: 3.1 Standard finetuning objective vs. OFT objective
3.2 Equation of OFT with layer‑shared orthogonal matrices
3.3 How to initialise the orthogonal matrix (identity)
3.4 Scope of application: fully‑connected layers, attention weights, optionally convolutional layers
3.5 Back‑propagation and gradient flows through the orthogonal matrix

outline.description: Extends OFT by adding an explicit radius constraint that keeps the orthogonal matrix close to the identity, improving stability.
subtopics: 4.1 Motivating the radius constraint
4.2 COFT objective formulation
4.3 Practical enforcement via Cayley‑parameterised Q and projected gradient descent
4.4 Hyper‑parameter ε: trade‑off between flexibility and fidelity
4.5 Empirical analysis of ε on stability and performance

outline.description: Explains computational strategies that make OFT practical for large diffusion networks.
subtopics: 5.1 Why simple Gram–Schmidt is infeasible
5.2 Cayley transform and its computational advantage
5.3 Limitations: special orthogonal group (determinant +1)
5.4 Block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices: formulation and parameter counting
5.5 Optional block sharing for extreme parameter reduction
5.6 Comparison with LoRA’s low‑rank approach

outline.description: Adds a diagonal scaling matrix to OFT, retaining hyperspherical energy while providing extra flexibility.
subtopics: 6.1 Motivation for per‑neuron magnitude scaling
6.2 Forward‑pass modification with matrix D
6.3 Relationship to classical OFT
6.4 Empirical gains and computational cost

outline.description: Details the practical steps needed to integrate OFT/COFT into popular diffusion pipelines.
subtopics: 7.1 Targeted layers for finetuning: attention matrices, FFNs, or any linear transform
7.2 Learning rates, optimisers, and regularisation
7.3 Training schedules: epochs, number of images, data augmentations
7.4 Ensuring orthogonality during optimisation
7.5 Post‑training inference: replacing weights by R·W₀ without extra overhead
7.6 Reproducibility tricks

outline.description: Presents quantitative and qualitative results demonstrating OFT/COFT’s advantage over DreamBooth and LoRA.
subtopics: 8.1 Experimental setup: Stable Diffusion v1.5, dataset, training curves

8.3 Quantitative metrics: DINO, CLIP‑I, CLIP‑T, LPIPS

8.5 Human evaluation study

outline.description: Demonstrates OFT/COFT on edge‑to‑image, segmentation‑to‑image, and landmark‑to‑face tasks.
subtopics: 9.1 Task definitions and datasets (COCO, ADE20K, CelebA‑HQ)

9.5 Quantitative results and comparative tables

outline.description: Synthesises the benefits and limitations of OFT/COFT relative to other finetuning frameworks.
subtopics: 10.1 Parameter efficiency versus generalisation

outline.description: Summarises the contributions, highlights the practical impact, and emphasises the broader significance of manipulating neuron angles for generative control.
